----- chunk 1 of 6 · LatticeRank · Phase 2 · 591 chars -----
LatticeRank. Four minutes: how we register a wafer image, and when we refuse. One reference image. One search image. The structure repeats, so hundreds of places look like the answer. Four candidates here. Their correlation scores are almost identical, but only one is the true site. Choose wrong and the defect location, the overlay number, and the tool decision move with it. In a lattice, similarity is cheap. What matters is the evidence that breaks the repetition. Wrong cell, and the error is a whole period. Not a blur. So: keep every plausible candidate, and commit only on evidence.

----- chunk 2 of 6 · 02 · V1 to V2 · 533 chars -----
Phase one handed us the scale, promised the reference was present, and asked only for x and y. That version one matcher still picks the site. Phase two extends it. Phase two takes the training wheels off. Zoom, rotation and presence are all unknown now. Zoom lands anywhere from eight to twelve times. Rotation, within five degrees. One pair in five contains no true instance. Two hundred pairs, four sets. So the output row grows: x, y, theta, scale, found, and a calibrated score. Report a pose, reject absences, and fail out loud.

----- chunk 3 of 6 · 03 · How it works · 696 chars -----
One pipeline. Seven stages carry a raw pair through to a single decided row. Decode safely. Band-pass out the drift and charging. Sweep poses, correlate, rank, refine, then decide. Version two's new work is the last two stages: presence and confidence. Here are the same stages again, this time with the image each one actually sees. Decode, band-pass, then nine scales crossed with five rotations. That is forty-five full-image correlations per pair. The best peak is refined to subpixel. Then: is it present, and how far do we trust it? Forty-five hypotheses on a grid. Hard-coding the disclosed bounds is allowed, so we do. Found and score are different questions. A present pair can be wrong.

----- chunk 4 of 6 · 04 · Data and contract · 318 chars -----
Our generator is a controlled lab: known poses, audited labels, deliberate damage. Twenty audited sample pairs: sixteen present, four with no true instance. Exactly one row per pair. A missing row scores zero, so failures still write one. Read found first, then score. One triggers a re-scan; the other decides action.

----- chunk 5 of 6 · 05 · How to run · 448 chars -----
Install, then one command. Python three eleven, four CPU cores, no GPU, no network, weights in the zip. This is the real thing, not a mock-up. The smoke input ships inside the zip: two pairs, DRAM and FinFET. It loads the models, sweeps the pose grid for each pair, refines the winner, then writes the CSV. Two pairs, six point four seconds, and both were found. Both rows present, both localized. And score is a probability, not a raw correlation.

----- chunk 6 of 6 · 06 · Results · 248 chars -----
On the official twenty-pair sample: seventy-nine point one four out of eighty-five. Frozen solver, nothing tuned. The published baseline averages zero point eight. We average zero point nine seven. Register, decide, and report how much to trust it.
